title: Handmade Tagliatelle with Brown Butter & Sage
short: Fresh egg pasta made together, in the simplest, most luxurious sauce.
keywords: Handmade Tagliatelle with Brown Butter & Sage, date night, dinner for two, playful, cozy
intro: Making pasta together is the ultimate cook-together date. Flour and eggs become silky dough in ten minutes of kneading; after a rest, one of you feeds the sheets through the machine while the other catches them. The sauce is barely a recipe: butter browned until nutty with crisp sage leaves.
why: It is an activity, not just a meal. You will make it together, laugh at the first wonky sheet, and eat something you could not buy.

ings.h: 200 g (1⅔ cups)
ings.i: '00' flour or all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting

ings.h: 60 g (4 tbsp)
40 g (½ cup)

steps.t: Mound the flour on a clean counter, make a deep well and crack the eggs into it with the salt. Beat the eggs with a fork, gradually pulling in flour from the walls until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy. If it sticks, dust with flour; if it cracks, wet your hands. Wrap and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Cut the dough in two. Flatten one piece and roll it through a pasta machine from the widest setting down to the second-thinnest, folding and re-rolling twice on the widest setting first. By hand, roll to 1–1.5 mm, thin enough to see your hand through it.
Dust the sheets with flour, fold loosely into a flat roll and cut into 6–8 mm ribbons. Toss with semolina and form loose nests.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta for 2–3 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. When it foams, add the sage and cook 3–4 minutes until the butter is hazelnut brown and the leaves are crisp.
Move the pasta into the butter with 60 ml (¼ cup) pasta water and toss until glossy. Add the Parmesan, lemon zest and pepper and toss again.

tips: Make it a two-person job: one cranks, one feeds and catches the sheets.
Fresh pasta cooks fast; taste after 90 seconds.
makeahead: Dough keeps wrapped in the fridge for 24 hours. Cut nests can be frozen on a tray and cooked from frozen (add 1 minute).
plating: Twist into a high nest, lay three crisp sage leaves on top, and finish with a final grating of cheese at the table.
zero: Sparkling apple juice with a sage leaf.

faq.q: Do I need a pasta machine?
faq.a: No. A rolling pin works; it just takes more muscle and patience.
